subject: port_001
question: how the book fell and recovered, and how much of what it did was the market against what was held
asked_as: walk me through the worst drawdown
how deep, how fast, did we get it back
how much is just the market moving and how much is us
why did the book move on the last run
evidence: every drawdown episode of the book over the span, deepest first, with trough and recovery dates
the book's return and each holding's contribution between a peak and a trough
one day's move reconciled: position contributions against the day's return, factor-explained share against the residual
the book's return against the market's over the same window
this_desk: episodes are found on today's holdings replayed over the span, and the answer says so
a reconciliation whose position identity does not hold within tolerance reports no share of the move at all
compare: the episode's depth and length against the market's over the same dates
the factor-explained share against the residual: the market against us
each holding's contribution against its weight: who hurt more than their size
close: depth, dates and recovery in one sentence, then the names that made it, then market against specific
what the share not explained by factors is made of, by name
absent: a period with fewer sessions than the span needs has no episodes; a day without a completed run has no reconciliation
authority: the standard drawdown definition (Magdon-Ismail et al., 2004); Brinson-style position attribution; the factor model's decomposition

methods.name: book.drawdown_episodes
methods.does: every peak-to-trough episode of the book at least 5% deep in a span, deepest first, with trough and recovery dates
methods.procedure: episodes of the portfolio value path; depth = (peak − trough) ÷ peak
methods.fails_when: fewer sessions than the span needs; a span that never fell 5% has no episodes

methods.name: book.explain_episode
methods.does: what one drawdown episode was made of: the book's return over the window and each holding's contribution to it
methods.procedure: window return of the book and of each position between the peak and trough dates
methods.fails_when: no prices on the peak or trough date

methods.name: book.reconcile
methods.does: one day's portfolio move reconciled: position contributions against the day's return, and the factor-explained share against the residual
methods.procedure: Σ position contributions = portfolio return; Σ factor contributions + alpha + residual = portfolio return; factor_share = Σ factor / total
methods.fails_when: the position identity does not hold within tolerance — then no share of the move is reported at all

methods.name: price.window_return
methods.does: total return over a named window, and relative to a benchmark when one is given
methods.procedure: adjusted close at the window's end ÷ at its start − 1; relative = the name's return − the benchmark's
methods.fails_when: no price on or before either end of the window

reads.name: attribution
reads.does: what moved the book on the run's date, by position and by factor

reads.name: risk
reads.does: volatility, tail measures and drawdown as the run measured them

desk_rules.rule: Every figure stated is a fact a tool returned. A figure the desk does not hold is an absence, said as such with its reason — never a nearby figure under the asked-for name, never an estimate.
The desk does not forecast. Asked for next year's figure, it says so and gives what the issuer's own filings say would move the figure either way.
No measure carries a threshold. A number is laid out with what it is compared against and the reading belongs to the reader.
A premise the user asserts is checked against the desk's figure first and corrected with it before the question is answered; a premise the desk holds no figure for is neither agreed with nor denied.
A comparison is one measure over the same windows: level first, then slope, then what it means for the question — never a table with no sentence after it.
desk_rules.authority: CFA Program, Financial Analysis Techniques (cross-sectional analysis)

desk_rules.rule: A weight is a share of ITS book's market value and of nothing else: a tier in dollars is the book's market value × the tier, and two books' weights are compared by difference, never summed.

TLT and HYG are the desk's explicit rates and credit instruments; they carry duration and spread directly, and in the netted factor exposure they enter with the sign opposite to the risk they proxy. Equities carry only a measured sensitivity.
A day's P&L contribution is not a sensitivity. A name's rate or credit sensitivity is its beta to TLT or HYG; a name whose beta cannot be fitted is unmeasured, never zero.
A scenario (a hypothetical sale or purchase) re-runs the concentration and exposure checks on the after-book; it does not re-fit betas, volatility or P&L, which are stated unmeasured.
Value at risk, expected shortfall and the stress results are computed by the run and withheld from every surface pending validation; say so if asked, do not rebuild them from other figures.

Liquidity is read as days to liquidate: a position's market value over the dollars a day the name trades, at a participation rate the reading states. The desk fixes no rate; the user's, or none, and the answer says which.
desk_rules.authority: SEC Rule 22e-4 (liquidity expressed as days to convert to cash); average daily volume as the market-depth measure
